description: Named comparison sides for tests/run.py (--a, --b). kind oracle: harness.oracle.serve(); kind fixture: the selftest site in tests/fixtures/site/ (fixture:<control> applies a control from tests/fixtures/controls.json); kind command: a server the harness starts in its own process group ({port} and {inspector_port} are free ports, never 8790; {dir} is the target's folder; {log_dir} the run's result folder; an argument "{wrangler}" is the repository's pinned wrangler, npm exec --no -- wrangler, or FEMTO_WRANGLER) and stops with every child; dir: the folder a command serves, which <name>:<path> replaces (dist:<path> serves any built folder exactly like dist); requires: a path that must exist first ({dir} filled in); env: environment variables for the command ({port}, {dir} and {log_dir} filled in). ready: the readiness hook run before collecting (oracle, static, none). max_documents: the most documents one server instance serves; a longer run is split into chunks, each with freshly started servers and browser sessions. same_origin: every document this side serves must load only same-origin resources (PLAN.md criterion 15); a cross-origin load in its Resource Timing entries fails the run outside the diff, where no registry entry applies. See tests/README.md, Modes.

oracle.about: The Remix site at tag remix-final, built with its locked toolchain and served by its own wrangler pages dev (tests/harness/oracle.py).
oracle.max_documents_why: wrangler 4.0.0's InspectorProxyWorker keeps every DevTools event of the worker (Network.enable: several per request) in runtimeMessageBuffer until a DevTools client connects, which none does. Its workerd isolate reached the V8 heap limit (about 1.4 GB) after about 1,240 page loads (43,000 requests) on 2026-10-30 (run p0-gate-self-cf, first attempt). A run therefore restarts every server, with fresh browser sessions, at most every 400 documents per server (tests/README.md, Rig notes).

dist.same_origin_why: PLAN.md criterion 15: every page loads only same-origin resources. The harness reads each document's own network log (Resource Timing), so a script that only displays a CDN URL passes and a fetch() or inserted <link> to another origin fails, whatever builds the URL.
dist.about: The static site: wrangler pages dev dist (or dist:<path>, any built folder), with the wrangler pinned in package.json. Phase 1 points side B here.
dist.env_why: wrangler writes a debug log on every run; WRANGLER_LOG_PATH keeps it in the run's result folder instead of ~/Library/Preferences/.wrangler/logs.
dist.dir_why: dist:<path> serves another built folder (a relative path is read from the repository root) exactly like dist: the same wrangler, options, readiness and same-origin rule, so several agents can each compare their own build at once.
dist.command_why: {wrangler} is npm exec --no -- wrangler, the wrangler pinned in package.json (--no never downloads one; targets.py checks node_modules/wrangler against the exact pin first). --persist-to gives each server its own state folder in the run's folder, so concurrent servers never share .wrangler/state.
